reference_description: The bar chart illustrates the comparison of perplexity values of "Per-Output" and "Per-Layer" at different sparsity rates.The horizontal axis labeled "Sparsity rates", ordered sequentially from 10% to 80%, in increments of 10%. The vertical axis labeled "Perplexity", with a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^1 to 10^3, marked with regularly spaced tick labels at intervals corresponding to powers of 10. The chart features pair of bars for each sparsity rate with blue bar followed by orange bar, with blue bars representing Per-Output and orange bars representing Per-Layer. The approximate perplexity values of the bars increase with higher sparsity rates, starting from around 2 at 10% sparsity, and approaching 10^3 as sparsity reaches 80%. The values remains below 10^2 till 70% sparsity. At 70% and 80% sparsity, the bars exhibit a notable increase in height compared to the lower sparsity rates. At 60% the orange bar is slightly above 10^1 while the blue bar is still below 10^1. At 50%, 60%, 70% and 80% the orange bars are taller than the blue bars. The bars are not sorted in any particular order beyond the increasing sparsity rate. A legend positioned in the top-left corner of the figure defines each bar with "Per-Output" or "Per-Layer" and it's color.
